html:
The Spanish transition to democracy took place between the death of Franco in November 1975 and the election of a Socialist government in 1982.

Franco had named Juan Carlos de Borbón as his successor as king. Instead of keeping the dictatorship, Juan Carlos and his prime minister Adolfo Suárez dismantled it. Parties, including the Communists, were legalised, free elections were held in 1977, and the constitution of 1978 made Spain a democratic parliamentary monarchy with regional autonomy. An amnesty law closed the books on the crimes of the civil war and the dictatorship.

On 23 February 1981 Civil Guards seized parliament in an attempted coup, but the king spoke against it on television and it failed. Spain joined NATO in 1982 and the European Community in 1986. Its peaceful transition, like Portugal's Carnation Revolution, became a model. See Spain.
sum: The Spanish transition to democracy took place between the death of Franco in November 1975 and the election of a Socialist government in 1982.
